collections.title: Lead with clarity
collections.description: Clear standards, stronger teams, and a bias toward solving.

collections.title: Choose what matters
collections.description: Priorities, tradeoffs, and decisions for the season you are in.

collections.title: Build earned confidence
collections.description: Use behavior, practice, and perspective to act through uncertainty.

quotes.text: life happens on the way to your goals. Not once you get there.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Success Is Who You Become, Behavior Beats Mindset, and Clarity Creates Speed | Ep. 374
quotes.context: Leila reflects on why progress and life happen during the process rather than at the finish line.

quotes.text: It really taught me that success is about who you become. It's about the character that you build.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Success Is Who You Become, Behavior Beats Mindset, and Clarity Creates Speed | Ep. 374
quotes.context: Leila describes success as the character built through a demanding process.

quotes.text: But different is created through the process, not this artificial ceremony of what you just did.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Success Is Who You Become, Behavior Beats Mindset, and Clarity Creates Speed | Ep. 374
quotes.context: Leila contrasts personal change through a process with the brief ceremony of an outcome.

quotes.text: It is more valuable and you will learn more if you practice being successful than if you visualize being successful.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Success Is Who You Become, Behavior Beats Mindset, and Clarity Creates Speed | Ep. 374
quotes.context: Leila favors practicing successful behavior over relying only on visualization.

quotes.text: clarity creates speed. Speed leads to progress. Progress leads to momentum, and momentum leads to success.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Success Is Who You Become, Behavior Beats Mindset, and Clarity Creates Speed | Ep. 374
quotes.context: Leila links clear direction with the momentum created by consistent progress.

quotes.text: It is okay to feel unsure and you can still speak confidently. Those things can exist at the same time.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: 5 Ways to Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Ep. 376
quotes.context: Leila separates the internal feeling of uncertainty from the external choice to communicate clearly.

quotes.text: I can't always control my thoughts, but I can control how I act.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: 5 Ways to Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Ep. 376
quotes.context: Leila explains why behavior can remain intentional even when thoughts are difficult to control.

quotes.text: The best leaders and the most confident people that I know ask the most questions, listen the most, probably do more listening and less talking in meetings.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: 5 Ways to Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Ep. 376
quotes.context: Leila contrasts grounded confidence with dominating a room or talking over other people.

quotes.text: There's something you do every day where you can practice one of these things. Be very specific.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: 5 Ways to Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Ep. 376
quotes.context: Leila recommends attaching confidence practice to a specific recurring situation.

quotes.text: All skills are additional, whereas leadership is the only skill that multiplies.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Leaders Solve Instead of Complain, and Business Is Always Personal | Ep. 378
quotes.context: Leila explains why leadership multiplies the value of every other capability in a company.

quotes.text: So the best leaders I've recognized on a call when they bring me a problem, they spend about 10% of the time on the problem and 90% of the time on the possible solutions to solve it.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Leaders Solve Instead of Complain, and Business Is Always Personal | Ep. 378
quotes.context: Leila describes the problem-to-solution ratio she sees in effective leaders.

quotes.text: And in the moment when I'm dealing with the problem, I ask myself, am I focusing in my thoughts on the problem or on what I need to do next?
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Leaders Solve Instead of Complain, and Business Is Always Personal | Ep. 378
quotes.context: Leila shares a live self-audit for moving attention from an obstacle to the next action.

quotes.text: And the values you live your personal life by, whether you like it or not, become the values at which you operate your company.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Leaders Solve Instead of Complain, and Business Is Always Personal | Ep. 378
quotes.context: Leila connects a leader's personal conduct with the values that appear inside the company.

quotes.text: And it's funny because people say like values, like values are what you do, not what you say.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Leaders Solve Instead of Complain, and Business Is Always Personal | Ep. 378
quotes.context: Leila emphasizes that values are visible in repeated behavior rather than stated intention.

quotes.text: A great leader hires people smarter than them.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Hire People Smarter Than You, Pick the Right People, and Adapt to Reality | Ep. 381
quotes.context: Leila opens with a standard for leaders who want the company and themselves to grow.

quotes.text: Just like you shortcut your way to making more money in investing by using other people's money, you can shortcut your way to success in business by using other people's brains.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Hire People Smarter Than You, Pick the Right People, and Adapt to Reality | Ep. 381
quotes.context: Leila compares hiring specialized talent to using leverage in investing.

quotes.text: The goal is to hire people who beat you at what you were doing, who are better than you at what you were doing.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Hire People Smarter Than You, Pick the Right People, and Adapt to Reality | Ep. 381
quotes.context: Leila says a strong hire should raise the standard of work the leader previously owned.

quotes.text: The best leaders learn to adapt to that change and they come out stronger on the other end.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Hire People Smarter Than You, Pick the Right People, and Adapt to Reality | Ep. 381
quotes.context: Leila frames adaptation as a defining response to fear, change, and uncertain conditions.

quotes.text: Do I argue with reality or do I respond to reality?
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: Hire People Smarter Than You, Pick the Right People, and Adapt to Reality | Ep. 381
quotes.context: Leila offers a question for checking whether a leader is adapting or resisting current conditions.

quotes.text: It's usually been because I haven't had clarity around what the number one priority is, or I felt like I've had to balance like 17 things at once.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: How to Win the Season You’re Currently In | Ep. 383
quotes.context: Leila connects dissatisfaction with a lack of clarity about the current number-one priority.

quotes.text: But I think that it is so freeing once you do it, because the irony of it is that not deciding is still a decision.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: How to Win the Season You’re Currently In | Ep. 383
quotes.context: Leila argues that avoiding a decision is itself a consequential choice.

quotes.text: A decision is not a decision unless you have to sacrifice.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: How to Win the Season You’re Currently In | Ep. 383
quotes.context: Leila defines a real decision by the options and investments it requires a person to give up.

quotes.text: you don't need to feel guilty for the fact that not everything is a fucking priority right now. I actually think there's something like really freeing about that because if everything's a priority, then nothing is.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: How to Win the Season You’re Currently In | Ep. 383
quotes.context: Leila explains why a season needs an explicit hierarchy instead of treating everything as equally urgent.

quotes.text: If you can just make a choice about what matters most to you right now and accept that that means other things won't get as much time and attention or they will have less rather than none. I think a lot more people would be a lot happier.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: How to Win the Season You’re Currently In | Ep. 383
quotes.context: Leila closes by asking people to choose what matters in the present season and accept the tradeoff.

quotes.text: You can have empathy for somebody yet not take responsibility for their feelings.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: You're Not Empathetic. You're Just Scared to Disappoint People | Ep. 384
quotes.context: Leila distinguishes empathy from assuming responsibility for another person's emotional response.

quotes.text: If you say yes, because you're worried about the reaction someone's gonna give if you say no, then it's all of a sudden like, what I'm really worried about is how they're gonna deal with their emotions.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: You're Not Empathetic. You're Just Scared to Disappoint People | Ep. 384
quotes.context: Leila explains how anticipated reactions can quietly turn a boundary into an unwanted yes.

quotes.text: people treat the feeling of guilt as evidence that they've done something wrong.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: You're Not Empathetic. You're Just Scared to Disappoint People | Ep. 384
quotes.context: Leila challenges the assumption that feeling guilty is proof a decision was wrong.

quotes.text: What if feeling guilty, you could feel guilty whether you did wrong or right?
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: You're Not Empathetic. You're Just Scared to Disappoint People | Ep. 384
quotes.context: Leila reframes guilt as a feeling that can accompany either a right or wrong choice.

quotes.text: And that's okay because I have so much more freedom in my life and I feel like I'm living my life in a way that is in accordance with my values and not in accordance with other people's feelings.
quotes.author: Leila Hormozi
quotes.sourceTitle: You're Not Empathetic. You're Just Scared to Disappoint People | Ep. 384
quotes.context: Leila describes the freedom that comes from making decisions according to her values.
